answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must bind identities through cryptographic attestation chains and zero-knowledge proofs. New nodes cannot simply forge credentials or rely on a fable of unverified reputational history. Instead, protocol collateral demands scale superlinearly: registration stakes increase exponentially with concurrent cluster size, as O(2^k). This ensures exponential capital exhaustion across any attacking swarm, effectively burying malicious entities beneath prohibitive costs like shifting dune sands.
